bug_semantics: An attacker-controlled template containing thousands of nested parentheses drives Parser.ParseParenthesis to call ExpectAndParseExpression, which re-enters ParseExpression once per nesting level. In the affected 6.5.8 tree, ParserOptions.ExpressionDepthLimit is nullable and defaults to null, so EnterExpression's HasValue-gated check is skipped and recursion can exhaust the CLR thread stack; StackOverflowException then terminates the hosting process. The nominal 6.6.0 change supplies a fallback limit but only logs an error and continues descending, so the effective repair is the later change that aborts parsing at the configured limit and also checks remaining execution-stack capacity.
flaw_origin: Root commit 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589 first added the recursive parenthesis path in src/Textamina.Scriban/Parsing/Parser.Expressions.cs:464-481, specifically ParseParenthesis calling ExpectAndParseExpression at line 469, without any expression-recursion guard. Later history renamed/moved the file and added an optional ExpressionDepthLimit check, but did not create the recursion flaw; the same unbounded parenthesis call chain already exists in the root tree.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object has human author Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, the same human committer, message 'Initial version', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI-attribution trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory: https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-wgh7-7m3c-fx25 and its repository API record https://api.github.com/repos/scriban/scriban/security-advisories/GHSA-wgh7-7m3c-fx25 describe attacker-supplied deeply nested expressions, fatal StackOverflowException process termination, affected version 6.5.8, and patched version 6.6.0. The assigned alias is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x4hp-vj3w-6w2m (CVE-2026-74795).

git log 6.5.8 -L 953,970:src/Scriban/Parsing/Parser.Expressions.cs traces the vulnerable ParseParenthesis body through moves and edits to root commit 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589, where the file was newly added from /dev/null. At that BIC, src/Textamina.Scriban/Parsing/Parser.Expressions.cs:133 dispatches '(' to ParseParenthesis, lines 464-481 define it, and line 469 recursively calls ExpectAndParseExpression.

Direct-parent verification: git rev-list --parents -n 1 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589 returns only the commit itself, and git cat-file -p shows no parent header. It is the repository root, so there is no direct-parent tree and the vulnerable source lines are absent from the empty prehistory; introducer_parent is therefore null and introducer_parent_absent is true.

Affected-tree verification: tag 6.5.8 resolves to b640147b792c41aa3756b463673c741e46c44470 and contains the BIC. In that tree, src/Scriban/Parsing/Parser.Expressions.cs:953-970 retains the recursive ParseParenthesis call (line 958); lines 1178-1181 enforce depth only when Options.ExpressionDepthLimit.HasValue; and src/Scriban/Parsing/ParserOptions.cs:20 declares nullable ExpressionDepthLimit without an initializer.

Declared-boundary finding: tag 6.6.0 resolves exactly to b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 (https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7), matching the first-party advisory's patched version. That commit changes EnterExpression to Options.ExpressionDepthLimit ?? 250 at src/Scriban/Parsing/Parser.Expressions.cs:1178-1182, but the limit branch only calls non-fatal LogError and sets _isExpressionDepthLimitReached; it neither returns nor throws, so recursive descent continues. Parser.cs:450-490 confirms ordinary LogError only records HasErrors unless isFatal is true.

Effective fix: 8fdbd687bbe8f00085c4c4c5b2b3b8d529933949 (https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/8fdbd687bbe8f00085c4c4c5b2b3b8d529933949) changes src/Scriban/Parsing/Parser.Expressions.cs:1209-1231 to call RuntimeHelpers.EnsureSufficientExecutionStack, log fatal errors, and throw FatalParserException both near stack exhaustion and when ExpressionDepthLimit is exceeded; Parser.cs catches that sentinel at the top parse boundary. Its added TestParser.cs:930-952 cases explicitly exercise 10,000 nested parentheses/arrays/objects/unary expressions and the same liquid-parenthesis path.

Version membership: git merge-base --is-ancestor proves 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589 is in 6.5.8 and b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 is in 6.6.0. The effective fix 8fdbd687bbe8f00085c4c4c5b2b3b8d529933949 is absent from 7.2.0 (7fdf19df7db01c5e57888c5cc31e4d05f3d75440) and present in 7.2.1 (d45f7f03c3407729da7fe663c180ce780adb9329), so source history does not substantiate the advisory's claimed effective 6.6.0 boundary even though the fix lands after that boundary.

BIC-only AI inspection: numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1 git cat-file -p 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589 shows tree 123692dfe743137eb23f1cfb70cff119c0858400, author and committer Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, and the message 'Initial version' with no trailers or AI/bot marker. No PR body, later commit, or fix authorship was used for attribution.
reasoning: The advisory PoC's causal path is the recursive parenthesis parser, not merely the later nullable option declaration. Line history reaches the first public repository commit, which created ParseParenthesis and its recursive ExpectAndParseExpression call without an expression-depth guard; all later option and file-organization changes inherited that mechanism. The BIC is a root commit rather than a move, refactor, revert, backport, or identifiable squash member, so no decomposition is available or required, and its no-parent commit object proves parent-tree absence. The official 6.5.8 affected tag contains both the recursion and a disabled-by-default nullable guard. The 6.6.0 boundary commit installs a default value but does not terminate recursion after recording the error; 8fdbd687bbe8f00085c4c4c5b2b3b8d529933949 is the smallest source commit that actually aborts the same deep-expression path and adds direct 10,000-level regression coverage. Finally, attribution is determined solely from the BIC commit object: it identifies a human author/committer and contains no AI marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
